# Quick visual explainers

An ELI5 page someone can send to a product manager or colleague: a quick way to understand an idea, a small investigation or a result without a presenter or specialist vocabulary. This is neither a miniature research paper nor a marketing page for the research.

Make the central relationship or change visible: the picture carries the explanation; text labels and qualifies it. Lead with the point in plain language. Use interaction or motion to reveal the relationship, not merely enliven the surrounding interface. Keep supporting evidence and important uncertainty reachable without making every reader traverse the full investigation. Short does not mean technically false.

An internal brief generally needs calmer framing than a public educational microsite. A large decorative hero, a report-shaped wall of prose, or a dashboard of findings is not the target merely because the output is HTML. Choose the arrangement that makes this particular result easy to grasp; there is no fixed section or animation count.

## Approved calibration pair

| Reference | What to study and borrow |
|---|---|
| [Good vs Great Animations — Emil Kowalski](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/good-vs-great-animations) | Animation article with embedded comparisons. Operate the origin-aware Options popup: the trigger, menu and short explanation share one local context. Borrow the experience-then-explanation pattern, not the technical vocabulary for a non-technical audience. |
| [Train, Test, and Validation Sets — MLU-Explain](https://mlu-explain.github.io/train-test-validation/) | Illustrated classification explainer: one cat-and-dog population becomes labeled, color-linked train, validation and test groups, then appears in an interactive model plot. Borrow continuity of the concrete example and labels that connect prose to the picture. |

## Closest initial anchor

[What happens when you flip a switch? — BKV](https://bkvenergy.com/flip-the-switch-on-texas-energy/) is an electricity-journey microsite: a switch introduction leads into numbered generation and transmission stages, connected machinery illustrations and Explore controls. Borrow the visible system connections and approachable language, not its oversized opening, marketing framing or motion intensity for an internal artifact.

These three are the approved set for this category. Keep the gap visible rather than promoting unapproved reports, case-study pages or unrelated examples to satisfy a numerical quota.
